sample_unit: dialogues (85 cases x 17 configurations x 5 models)
models_evaluated: five frontier LLMs (names not given in the provided text)

links.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy under perturbed patient inputs (fabricated or withheld information)
links.effect: Fabricating symptoms produced 1.7-3.4x larger accuracy drops than withholding information. Fabricating was significant across all five models (McNemar p<0.05). Worst-case drops ranged from 38.8 to 54.1 percentage points.
links.quote: we find a fundamental asymmetry: information pollution (fabricating symptoms) produces 1.7-3.4x larger accuracy drops than information deficit (withholding information), and fabricating is the only configuration achieving statistical significance across all five models (McNemar p < 0.05).

unlisted_practices: Graded, dose-response adversarial patient behavior benchmarking of LLM diagnostic dialogue
Testing inquiry strategy (exhaustive questioning) as a moderator of information deficit but not fabricated input

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark study (MedDialBench) evaluating the diagnostic robustness and safety of frontier LLMs against simulated adversarial and non-cooperative patient behaviors in medical dialogue.
